title: Entra ID Governance: Access Reviews, Entitlement Management and Lifecycle Workflows
description:
Access that is never reviewed keeps growing, and yearly recertifications end in rubber stamps. This episode shows identity architects, IAM and compliance teams how access packages, access reviews, lifecycle workflows and PIM in Microsoft Entra ID Governance work together as one event-driven system.
In this episode
00:00 – The thesis: governance is a behavior problem03:21 – The old model and the map of Entra ID Governance10:00 – Identity data and licensing17:01 – Entitlement management, access packages and guests33:40 – Access reviews that people actually complete47:10 – Lifecycle workflows: joiners, movers and leavers67:45 – Privileged access with PIM74:56 – One system: ownership, metrics, rollout and failure patterns
Key takeaways
Entra ID Governance works when it is designed around real behavior: named owners, safe defaults and review tasks small enough to finish.Access packages with expiry, scoped access reviews with recommendations and auto-apply, and lifecycle workflows driven by clean HR attributes replace the yearly cleanup.Privileged roles should be eligible and activated just in time through PIM, and the whole program should be rolled out in phases starting with data quality.
Worth quoting
“Attribute quality is the first architecture decision, not the last one. Most teams treat it as cleanup.” – Mirko Peters (12:35)
